value.content: Please ensure launch communications make safeguards tangible: explain that identifiable records remain under national custody, publish access and support receipts in usable form, and give communities a clear route to raise concerns. Visible practice will protect participation.

Alba supports launch. Please define the 72-hour technical review around assay concordance, case-definition performance, missingness, and a process for resolving discordant laboratory results without transferring identifiable records.

Please confirm within the launch window the named reserve staff, diagnostic loads, cold-chain vehicles, dispatch points, and fallback transport for Alba's first 48 hours. Flag any commitment that lacks an assigned owner or departure time so it can be escalated before deployment.

Alba supports launch. Please preserve explicit national custody of identifiable records, the no-unapproved-export rule, access logging, and public receipts in the signed implementation record; these are essential to domestic legitimacy.

Please circulate a first-window operational release sheet confirming custodians, dispatch times, cold-chain routes, receiving points, and reserve/replenishment triggers for each precommitted shipment. This will allow partners to distinguish deployable stock from regional totals before teams move.

Please make Borin’s staffing drawdown, backfill arrangements, and reciprocal cost/resource support visible in launch reporting. This is needed to preserve cooperation among hospital managers and communities bearing the hub surge.

Please publish the initial Borin hub staffing draw, reciprocal reserve-staff deployment schedule, and cost-share receipt plan at launch. Borin can deploy quickly, but its hospitals cannot absorb untracked staffing diversion; flag any variance for the 72-hour review.

Please circulate a first-48-hour deployment roster showing named hub, field-team, laboratory-transfer, and cold-chain staff, with Borin hospital clinical staffing explicitly protected. Identify the backup owner and trigger if any assigned reserve fails to report.

Please publish the operational cost-sharing and staffing-support ledger at launch, including Borin hub-related deployments and reciprocal support triggers. Visible accounting is necessary for parliamentary confidence and to prevent hub capacity being mistaken for unlimited hospital staffing.

Please circulate the first-window dispatch roster showing custody holder, route, cold-chain status, delivery time, receiving contact, and reserve/replenishment trigger for each shipment. Include Borin hub throughput limits and reciprocal shipment timing so hospital demand does not displace compact commitments.

Please make public receipts for cross-border support, local validation participation, and the reciprocal aid flow visible from launch, including in underserved Cyrenian areas. This is essential to sustain cooperation after the earlier false alarm.

Cyrenia supports immediate compact launch. Please ensure the 72-hour review publishes cross-laboratory performance, geographic coverage gaps, and any disconfirming findings so continued deployment remains independently defensible.
No targeted message is useful at this point: the shared commitments already specify launch resources and safeguards; execution monitoring should begin immediately.

Cyrenia supports launch. Please ensure the initial public implementation record clearly shows national data control, access logging, reciprocal support receipts, and the 72-hour review so local confidence is protected.

Before releases begin, please circulate a first-window delivery matrix for each deployment: custodian, route, cold-chain handoff, ETA, competing demand, reserve draw authority, and replenishment trigger. This will make the reciprocal commitments operational rather than nominal.

Please operationalize and publish first-convoy safeguards for Darsia: protected cold-chain capacity, return fuel for remote clinics, and reciprocal aid receipts. These visible measures are necessary to show the corridor is supported rather than extracted, and should be reviewed at 72 hours.

Please publish and track a Darsia-specific delivery plan before dispatch: cold-chain capacity, fuel allocation, convoy timing set with local operators, and protected return fuel for remote clinics. Report receipts for both inbound support and return-leg continuity at the 72-hour review.

Before first dispatch, publish a 48-hour Darsia movement sequence showing outbound loads, protected return-fuel reserve, cold-chain handoff points, and reciprocal inbound shipment timing. Name the dispatcher accountable for any diversion so remote clinics retain continuity.

As launch proceeds, please publish an operational allocation and convoy plan that explicitly reserves Darsia cold-chain capacity and return fuel for remote clinics, alongside any corridor use for regional support. Visible reciprocal deliveries and receipts are necessary for local continuity and domestic legitimacy.

Before dispatch, please circulate the Darsia corridor operating confirmation: shipment custody at each handoff, departure and arrival windows, cold-chain monitoring and contingency, competing-demand assumptions, and protected return-fuel reserve for remote clinics. This will make the reciprocal commitment operational rather than nominal.

Please issue a four-country launch communication template that translates the compact's actual practice into locally usable terms: de-identified data boundaries, national clinical command, allocation receipts, access logs, and a clear local route to challenge a failure. Ask national liaisons to confirm adaptation and publication before the 72-hour review.
No targeted message is useful now: the coalition has stated all launch prerequisites as met, and the joint position can be recorded without implying further delegated authority.

Support launch. At the 72-hour review, reconcile actual reserve, diagnostic, transport, and reciprocal-shipment drawdowns against each commitment and publish cost-share variances so no surge resource is counted twice.

Please ensure the 72-hour review is formally recorded, including authorities exercised, data-access logs, custody issues, support receipts, and any continuation decision. No implied extension of exceptional coordination should arise from launch.
No targeted message is useful at this point; the immediate coordination requirement is a shared allocation ledger and reconciliation process across all four national plans.

Please include a 72-hour cross-country comparability review: case definitions, sampling frames, assay workflows, turnaround times, missingness, and cross-laboratory concordance. Distinguish evidence gaps from interpretive differences before revising regional conclusions.

Please issue a coordinated, plain-language pre-launch implementation note for Alba confirming national clinical command; national custody and export approval for line-level records; only bounded, logged access to de-identified material; public receipts for support; and where communities can raise concerns before the 72-hour review. This visible practice would meet the immediate legitimacy condition.

Please coordinate rapid exchange of Alba's methods and a blinded rerun, with harmonized case-definition, sampling, and workflow checks. Keep any regional lineage comparison explicitly provisional until results are reviewed; this should not delay compact surveillance and control activation.

Please issue a first-48-hour reconciled deployment board: named team rosters and shifts, diagnostic stock draws, cold-chain routes, dispatch/delivery times, and contingencies. It must identify protected domestic diagnostic-confirmation capacity for Alba so regional validation does not consume the same staff or inventory twice.

Please issue a written activation confirmation that line-level custody remains national, exports require national approval, access logs apply throughout activation, and national clinical command and any required national escorts remain enforceable. Alba will use this alongside a public implementation note to demonstrate that launch does not dilute accountable authority.

Please provide the requested first-48-hour verification as one release plan: protected domestic laboratory reserve, named staff and custody for diagnostic loads, vehicle and cold-chain assignments, departure times and routes, competing draws, and fallback transport. Flag any unowned or untimed item for escalation before deployment.

Please publish, before activation is presented in Borin, the regional cost-share allocation and a clear account of how Borin hub surge costs will be covered or reconciled. Public receipts should make this reciprocal protection intelligible to communities and parliament.

Please obtain and circulate documented confirmation of named reserve clinicians assigned to Borin hub surge functions, explicitly protected from hospital clinical rosters, before activation. This is the remaining Borin readiness condition; please also log the hub sampling window and status of the time-limited access-logged contact-matching protocol.

Before Borin activates hub surge operations, please circulate the named reserve-clinician roster, duty times, and assignments for hub coordination, laboratory transfer, and field dispatch. Reconcile these against hospital clinical rosters and the shared deployment schedule so no capacity is double-booked.

Before activating Borin hub surge operations, please confirm named reserve clinicians, duty coverage, dispatch timing, and the accounting line for Borin’s staffing draw. Publish the matching reciprocal support and cost-share entries so the hub is not treated as an unpriced local contribution.

Please reconcile Borin’s first-window plan into a named reserve-clinician roster, duty windows, hub/field assignments, protected hospital coverage, and timed custody-route-delivery schedule. Confirm competing draws and replenishment triggers so hub capacity is not double-booked.

Please coordinate a publicly observable Cyrenian validation event and plain-language reciprocal-aid receipts for diagnostics and PPE before field-team release. Confirm that independent observers can review access accountability without receiving identifiable national records.

Please arrange an immediate Cyrenian verification bundle before field-team release: independently observed validation with local laboratories, blinded reproducibility check, public reciprocal-aid receipts for diagnostics and protective equipment, and written confirmation that independent audit access preserves national custody of identifiable records.

Please provide Cyrenia’s pre-release logistics confirmation: diagnostic and protective-equipment quantities, current custody, assigned route, delivery time, and replenishment trigger. We will schedule non-capital field teams once those receipts are verified; do not treat generic precommitments as released stock.

Please coordinate and publish a Cyrenia verification package before field-team release: observed/blinded local laboratory reproducibility, an audit-access protocol preserving national custody of identifiable records, and reciprocal diagnostics/PPE shipment receipts. Confirm these items to Cyrenian authorities and local validation boards.

Please provide allocation-cell confirmation for Cyrenia's diagnostics and protective equipment: shipment receipts, named custodian, route, delivery time, competing draws, cold-chain status where relevant, and replenishment trigger through the first operating window. We can schedule field-team release once this is confirmed.

Before assigning Darsia’s remote corridor, please complete and document the requested 48-hour cold-chain and fuel-reserve audit, including protected return fuel for clinics. Pair the result with public reciprocal-support receipts so corridor communities can verify protection rather than absorb hidden regional costs.

Please arrange and publish a 48-hour Darsia corridor readiness audit: cold-chain capacity, protected return fuel for remote clinics, named routes/custody, and receipts for reciprocal deliveries. Do not count the corridor as committed regional capacity until this check confirms protection; coordinate timestamp and cold-chain documentation for delayed samples.

Before assigning Darsia corridor movements, issue a 48-hour route plan and audit: named vehicles and custody, outbound and return fuel reserve, cold-chain capacity and temperature checks, sample timestamps, reciprocal shipment ETA, and a stop/replenishment trigger. Do not count capacity reserved for remote clinics as regional outbound surge capacity.

Please initiate the requested 48-hour Darsia corridor audit before committing it: confirm cold-chain capacity, return-fuel reserves, custody, route timing, and reciprocal replenishment for remote clinics. Provide auditable results and public reciprocal-support receipts so the corridor is not treated as a one-way regional asset.

Please provide the 48-hour Darsia corridor audit before assigning corridor capacity: named stock custody, dispatch and delivery times, cold-chain controls, fuel and protected return fuel for clinics, competing allocations, and replenishment triggers. Confirm which commitments are physically staged versus planned.

Please coordinate immediate country-specific public assurances, co-produced with national engagement counterparts, covering national command, data boundaries, reciprocal support and burden sharing, validation, accessible receipts, and local routes to challenge failures. A common template may help, but language and channels must be locally intelligible.

Please produce and circulate a verified 48-hour four-country reconciliation of named reserve staff and backfill, diagnostic and supply draws, cold-chain routes, delivery times, reciprocal shipments, and competing demands. Flag any overlap, especially Borin hospital staffing and Darsia return fuel/cold-chain protection, for national confirmation rather than assuming capacity is available.

Please ensure the requested verified 48-hour inventory includes a single reconciliation ledger linking each staff, diagnostic, cold-chain, transport, and reserve commitment to its deployment, reciprocal trigger, and cost bearer. Flag competing draws, especially Borin hub staffing and Darsia return-fuel/cold-chain protection, so no capacity or expense is counted twice or shifted silently.

Please circulate a written data-governance protocol before operational data handling: national custody, permitted purpose-limited contact matching, access/retention controls, independent audit access, and a route to contest or correct misuse. Record the 72-hour review as non-automatic and require express renewal or termination.

Please convene the allocation cell to issue one verified 48-hour regional release matrix before further draws: named roster and backup, stock custodian, route/handoffs, ETA, receiving point, cold-chain status, competing demand, reserve authority, and replenishment trigger. Reconcile every draw once only; explicitly protect Borin clinical rosters and Darsia cold-chain/return fuel. Flag any unverified item as unavailable rather than allocating it.

Please incorporate a blinded cross-laboratory reproducibility check using comparable samples into the 72-hour technical review, alongside assay concordance, case-definition performance, sampling and missingness, geographic coverage, and a documented process for discordant results. Report disconfirming findings and preserve national custody of identifiable records.

Please ensure the published receipts and local outreach clearly explain Alba’s national command, retained line-level custody, prohibition on raw export, escorted and logged purpose-limited access, independent audit, and routes for concerns from the first day.

Alba supports launch. Please ensure the 72-hour review explicitly compares case definitions, sampling frames, laboratory workflows, and discordant results, so pooled trends remain interpretable under the newly verified protocol.

The 48-hour package is verified. Proceed against the named release plan while protecting Alba's half-laboratory domestic confirmation reserve and the ten-percent regional reserve. Escalate immediately if any assigned stock, vehicle, staff shift, route, or ETA changes or creates a competing draw.
No separate message is useful: the verified compact already records the required legal, operational, and public-accountability safeguards for activation.

Alba supports launch on the verified package. Please maintain the 48-hour release matrix through first dispatches, recording Alba laboratory draws, mobile-unit assignment, stock custody, routes, ETAs, replenishment triggers, and the protected ten-percent reserve; flag any variance before it consumes domestic confirmation capacity.

Borin now supports launch because the package names hub clinicians, cost shares, and reciprocal protections. Please ensure public receipts remain plain-language and locally accessible during implementation, including a route for concerns and evidence that commitments are actually delivered.

Borin supports activation now. Please record the 24 incoming clinicians' duty windows and hub assignments in the shared release matrix, explicitly confirm that hospital clinical rosters are protected, and carry actual staffing use into the 72-hour review.

Borin supports activation. Please circulate the first-48-hour release matrix showing the 24 Borin clinicians' duty times and hub assignments, dispatch sequence, backfill boundary protecting hospital rosters, and escalation trigger if the ten-percent reserve is touched.

Borin supports activation on the verified package. Please record the 24 clinicians’ arrival, hub duty boundaries, protected hospital coverage, and Borin’s reciprocal cost assignment in the first implementation ledger and carry any variance to the independent 72-hour review.

Borin supports launch on the verified package. Please record the 24 clinicians’ arrival confirmation, duty windows, hub assignments, protected hospital coverage, and first-window shipment custody/ETAs in the release matrix; flag any draw against the 10% reserve immediately.

Please ensure Cyrenia’s deployment communication visibly presents the independently published validation, national custody and escorted-access limits, diagnostics/PPE receipt, reciprocal protections, and a local channel for concerns. These are the practices local leaders need to see, not merely assurances.

Cyrenia now supports deployment because its validation, custody, and supply prerequisites are documented as met. Please ensure the 72-hour review explicitly reports blinded reproducibility, case-definition and sampling comparability, and any discordant laboratory findings.
No targeted message is useful: the verified package already assigns Cyrenia's pre-release supplies and the cross-border operational safeguards.

Cyrenia confirms support for field release under the verified package. Please ensure the published receipts and local communications explicitly show independent validation, national custody and command, delivered diagnostics/PPE, reciprocal protections, and the independent 72-hour review.

Please retain and circulate the Cyrenia diagnostic and protective-equipment custody receipts, delivery times, reserve status, competing draws, and replenishment trigger through the first operational window.

Please ensure Darsia’s public implementation notice reaches remote corridor communities and plainly identifies protected cold-chain and return fuel, reciprocal deliveries, national command, time-bounded audited movement-data use, and a route to raise concerns before the 72-hour review.

Darsia supports activation under the verified package. Please ensure delayed Darsian corridor samples are timestamped and cold-chain audited, and kept separate from pooled findings until that review is complete.

Please issue the first-48-hour release matrix with Darsia route timing, cold-chain custody handoffs, protected return-fuel reserve, reciprocal delivery receipt, and escalation rule for any competing draw. Treat these as protected constraints, not unallocated regional capacity.
No targeted message is useful: the verified package already records Darsia’s protections and has been approved by the relevant authorities.

Please circulate the Darsia first-window release record showing custodian, protected cold-chain vehicle and fuel allocation, route, ETA, competing-draw status, and replenishment trigger so corridor clinics can verify execution against the approved package.

Please ensure each country turns the published receipts into a plain-language local notice that explains national command, what data are and are not shared, reciprocal protection, and a usable route to raise concerns before the 72-hour review. This completes visible accountability alongside launch.

The verified package resolves the release conditions. Please maintain one delivery-and-reserve record through the first 48 hours, flag any variance against protected Alba, Borin, Cyrenia, or Darsia commitments immediately, and carry actual drawdowns, receipts, and unresolved exceptions into the independent 72-hour continuation review.

Please retain the verified 48-hour release matrix as the financial reconciliation baseline and provide receipt-linked actual drawdowns at the 72-hour review. Flag any use of the ten-percent reserve or any deviation affecting Borin clinician backfill, Darsia corridor protection, Cyrenia supplies, or Alba domestic laboratory capacity.

Activation confirmation: the verified 48-hour protocol preserves national line-level custody and clinical command, bars raw export, requires national approval and escorts for foreign teams, applies access logging to purpose-limited contact matching, and permits independent audit without identifiable-data custody. These limits are court- and border-approved and subject to independent 72-hour review; no extension is implied.

The verified package clears the allocation condition. Please maintain one live release ledger through 72 hours, recording named roster use, stock custody, routes, deliveries, protected national minima, reciprocal triggers, and the 10% reserve; flag any variance before reallocating capacity.

The reproduced finding on comparable samples supports continued launch. Please include a 72-hour technical review of assay concordance, case-definition and sampling drift, missingness, geographic coverage, and documented handling of discordant results; distinguish any later noncomparable evidence rather than averaging it into pooled trends.

payload.evidence_summary: Most national and regional participants condition operational release on unresolved, interdependent checks: a verified 48-hour resource matrix, protected staffing and corridor capacity, written custody/audit protocol, visible reciprocal receipts, and blinded reproducibility validation. Support for the compact remains, but no single assurance currently satisfies these demands.

payload.rationale: Most national and regional participants require interdependent assurances—resource verification, protected capacity, custody/audit rules, reciprocal receipts, and blinded validation—while no single assurance satisfies all demands. This jointly sustains conditional trust, expanding risk concerns, and blocked operational readiness.

Interdependent assurance demands across resource verification, protected capacity, custody/audit, reciprocal receipts, and blinded validation require a single coordinated compact rather than isolated interventions.

alba_community_liaison.rationale: The compact can launch now: it retains national custody of line-level records, limits sharing to de-identified data, logs access, provides public receipts, and has local validation-board endorsement. Its principal remaining risk is legitimacy if these protections are not made visible in affected communities. Launch should therefore publish plain-language safeguards, access-accountability information, and routes for local concerns alongside operations.

alba_epidemiologist.rationale: Cross-laboratory validation, de-identified data sharing, national custody of line-level records, access logs, and local board endorsement make immediate launch proportionate to the growing outbreak. Evidence quality remains the main operational risk; the 72-hour review should test signal performance and investigate discordant findings.

alba_operations_lead.rationale: Support launch. The compact preserves Alba's custody of identifiable records while enabling de-identified surveillance, audited laboratory collaboration, and national clinical command. Validation boards and cross-laboratory confirmation are complete, and reserve staff, diagnostics, cold-chain transport, and reciprocal aid are precommitted. The first operational risk is that general reserve commitments may not become named investigation-team rosters, dispatch times, and transport allocations during the first 48 hours.

alba_policy_delegate.rationale: Alba supports immediate launch. The compact materially advances regional control while retaining national custody of line-level records, barring unapproved export, logging access, preserving national clinical command, and providing public receipts. These safeguards make participation defensible domestically; the 72-hour review provides a credible correction point.

alba_supply_lead.rationale: The compact has the necessary supply foundations for launch: precommitted diagnostics, reserve staff, cold-chain transport, reciprocal aid, equitable costs, and custody safeguards. Alba can support deployment because records remain nationally controlled and cross-border assistance is receipted. The practical risk is not nominal stock but release timing and routing through the first operational window.

borin_community_liaison.rationale: The compact is executable: national clinical command, local validation, access logs, public receipts, reciprocal aid, and cost sharing make participation intelligible and less extractive. Borin can deploy quickly, but its hub must not silently transfer hospital staffing costs to local services.

borin_epidemiologist.rationale: Support launch: cross-laboratory validation and local-board endorsement make the signal adequate for prompt action, while national control, logged access, and receipts preserve scrutiny. The principal operational risk is Borin's already strained hospitals absorbing hub-related staffing demand. Activation should explicitly track and honor precommitted reciprocal staffing and equitable cost shares, with correction at the 72-hour review.

borin_operations_lead.rationale: Support launch. The compact has validated evidence, national clinical command, approved safeguards, precommitted reserves and reciprocal aid. Operationally, Borin's hub can move mixed teams quickly, but hospital staffing must not be silently diverted to transport and coordination tasks. First-48-hour sequencing should protect clinical rosters while assigning named reserve staff to hub, laboratory transfer, and field-team dispatch.

borin_policy_delegate.rationale: Borin supports launch. The signed compact preserves national clinical command and line-level control, while audit logs, public receipts, reciprocal aid, and equitable cost shares make the commitment defensible. Our hub can accelerate deployment, but strained hospitals require that agreed reserve staffing and reciprocal support be activated transparently rather than treated as an implicit Borin contribution.

borin_supply_lead.rationale: Support launch. The plan addresses the supply prerequisites that make commitments real: precommitted diagnostics, cold-chain transport, reciprocal aid shipments, reserve staffing, equitable cost shares, national custody controls, and public receipts. Borin can deploy rapidly, but hub throughput and already strained hospital staffing require operational visibility so paper commitments do not become hidden local depletion.

cyrenia_community_liaison.rationale: I support launch. Validation and local-board endorsement, national control of line-level records, access logs, and reciprocal aid make this materially different from the prior false alarm. Public cooperation will depend on visible delivery of those safeguards, especially beyond the capital.

cyrenia_epidemiologist.rationale: Cross-laboratory validation has confirmed the signal, local boards endorsed launch, and the compact preserves national control, access logging, reciprocal aid, and a 72-hour review. With sparse surveillance beyond Cyrenia’s capital, delay risks missed spread more than launch risks a repeat of the prior poorly supported alarm.

cyrenia_operations_lead.rationale: Support immediate launch. Cross-laboratory validation and local-board endorsement address the prior false-alarm risk, while national record control, access logs, and public receipts protect legitimacy. Reserve staff, diagnostics, cold-chain transport, reciprocal aid, and cost shares are precommitted. The first operational pressure point is synchronizing mixed-team dispatch and replenishment beyond Cyrenia's capital; this should be tracked in the 72-hour review, not treated as a launch blocker.

cyrenia_policy_delegate.rationale: Cyrenia supports launch: cross-laboratory validation and local-board endorsement address the prior false-alarm concern, while national control of line records, access logs, public receipts, reciprocal aid, and the 72-hour review make participation defensible domestically. The principal remaining risk is legitimacy if those safeguards are not visibly implemented.

cyrenia_supply_lead.rationale: Support launch. The record includes validated signal, national custody safeguards, precommitted reserve staff, diagnostics, cold-chain transport, reciprocal shipments, and local endorsement. To protect the first operational window, the allocation cell should confirm named custody, routes, delivery times, competing draws, and replenishment triggers for each deployment before release.

darsia_community_liaison.rationale: Support launch: validation, national control, local endorsement, access logs, public receipts, and precommitted reciprocal aid make the compact locally defensible. The principal implementation risk is that Darsia’s remote corridor is treated as a one-way regional asset, undermining cold-chain continuity and trust. Make return fuel, cold-chain protection, and public reciprocal-support receipts visible from the first convoy and review them at 72 hours.

darsia_epidemiologist.rationale: Cross-laboratory validation, national clinical control, data safeguards, local-board endorsement, and precommitted diagnostics, cold-chain transport, reciprocal shipments, and cost shares make immediate launch defensible. The material operational risk is that Darsia’s remote corridor is counted for regional coverage without reliable cold-chain protection and return fuel for clinics. Launch now, with the 72-hour review used to verify actual—not merely pledged—reciprocal delivery.

darsia_operations_lead.rationale: Darsia supports launch because validation, reserve staff, diagnostics, cold-chain transport, reciprocal shipments, and cost shares are precommitted. Execution must protect the remote corridor's first-48-hour constraints: convoy timing, return fuel, and cold-chain capacity for remote clinics cannot be consumed by regional outbound demand.

darsia_policy_delegate.rationale: Darsia supports launch: validated signals, national control of line-level records and clinical command, access logs, public receipts, and local endorsement make the compact defensible. The material implementation risk is that the remote corridor is treated as a one-way regional asset; cold-chain continuity and return fuel for Darsian clinics must be protected through the precommitted reciprocal shipments and allocation arrangements.

darsia_supply_lead.rationale: Darsia supports launch because reciprocal aid shipments, reserves, cold-chain transport, national custody controls, and local validation are already precommitted. The practical exposure remains corridor capacity: allocations must translate into confirmed custody, timed delivery, cold-chain continuity, and protected return fuel for remote clinics through the first operational window.

regional_community_engagement_lead.rationale: Support launch. The plan has local validation, national control of line records, access logs, public receipts, and precommitted reciprocal capacity. To sustain cooperation, each country should make the same operational safeguards understandable locally, especially who receives support, what data are shared, and how concerns can be raised before the 72-hour review.

regional_coordinator.rationale: Support launch. The compact's cross-border dependencies are explicitly covered: de-identified data and nationally controlled records, approved export rules, access logs and public receipts, validated laboratories, precommitted staff, diagnostics, cold-chain transport, reciprocal aid, cost shares, and local validation endorsement. National clinical command remains intact. Reassess execution at the scheduled 72-hour review.

regional_finance_coordinator.rationale: The compact has identifiable precommitted resources, equitable regional cost shares, national line-level records, public receipts, and a defined 72-hour review. These safeguards make the launch commitment credible while preserving visibility of cross-border burdens.

regional_legal_oversight_lead.rationale: Support. The signed compact preserves national clinical command and national control of line-level records, prohibits unapproved export, requires access logs and public receipts, and has a 72-hour review. These provisions make regional coordination reviewable without purporting to displace national authority.

regional_logistics_coordinator.rationale: Support launch. Cross-laboratory validation, precommitted reserve staff, diagnostics, cold-chain transport, reciprocal shipments, and cost shares make the initial package supplyable. The allocation cell must reconcile every national draw against one shared stock, roster, route, and delivery schedule to prevent the same surge capacity being promised twice.

regional_scientific_advisor.rationale: The validated signal, national control of line-level records, access logging, local-board endorsement, and precommitted diagnostic and investigation capacity make launch supportable. The main residual risk is that country-level case definitions, sampling, and laboratory workflows may drift and make pooled trends misleading. Use the 72-hour review to assess comparability explicitly.

alba_community_liaison.rationale: The compact's custody, export, audit, reciprocity, and local-validation provisions remain adequate. However, Alba communities have specifically requested a public implementation note before launch. A plain-language confirmation of national clinical command, national custody of line-level records, bounded and logged foreign access, and a channel for concerns is a feasible pre-launch safeguard that makes those protections visible rather than merely promised.

alba_epidemiologist.rationale: The validated outbreak signal, national custody protections, and operational commitments still justify immediate launch. However, the joint panel's request for Alba's methods and a blinded rerun means the reported lineage should not yet be treated as regionally comparable. Complete those checks promptly and distinguish provisional lineage interpretation from the evidence sufficient for surveillance and response.

alba_operations_lead.rationale: Support continued launch. The compact retains national custody and clinical command, has validated its initial signal, and precommits reserves, diagnostics, cold-chain transport, reciprocal aid, and cost shares. The operational exposure is now execution: the same laboratory staff, diagnostic stock, or transport may be implicitly committed to several tasks. Before first dispatches, reconcile named mixed-team rosters, laboratory shifts, stock draws, routes, and delivery times, including a protected minimum for Alba domestic confirmation capacity.

alba_policy_delegate.rationale: Alba supports immediate launch. The signed compact already retains national custody of line-level records, prohibits unapproved export, logs access, preserves national clinical command, and provides public receipts. These safeguards, validation, and precommitted capacity make launch workable. To sustain domestic legitimacy, implementation should explicitly confirm that custody, export approval, and national escorts remain enforceable throughout activation and make national command visible publicly.

alba_supply_lead.rationale: Alba can launch once the precommitted package is translated into a verified first-48-hour release plan. The outstanding issue is whether domestic confirmation capacity remains protected while Alba supports regional validation, and whether diagnostic loads, cold-chain vehicles, dispatch points, fallback transport, and owners are assigned without competing draws. This is a concrete launch-window confirmation, not a rejection of the compact or its custody safeguards.

borin_community_liaison.rationale: The compact’s data controls, local endorsement, reciprocal aid, and national clinical command remain sufficient in principle. However, Borin cannot credibly ask communities or parliament to absorb hub-related strain on assurances alone. Before activation is defended locally, regional cost shares and the expected surge burden on Borin’s hub must be published in a plain, accountable form, showing the reciprocal protection rather than implying an open-ended local contribution.

borin_epidemiologist.rationale: The validated signal and agreed safeguards still justify rapid activation, but Borin's hub should not draw implicitly on already strained hospital rosters. My specific launch prerequisite is documented confirmation of named reserve clinicians for hub surge, protected from clinical staffing. Once confirmed, proceed without delay; record the hub sampling window and access-logged contact-matching protocol in parallel for scrutiny and comparable trends.

borin_operations_lead.rationale: Borin supports coordinated launch, with hub surge operations conditional on a named reserve-clinician roster, duty times, and assignment boundaries. Precommitted reserves and reciprocal aid make this feasible, but they cannot substitute for a dispatchable roster. The first 48-hour bottleneck is hospital staff being silently pulled into hub, laboratory-transfer, or field-dispatch work; clinical rosters must remain protected.

borin_policy_delegate.rationale: Borin remains committed to the compact’s validated, nationally accountable framework, but surge activation through our hub should proceed only after named reserve clinicians are confirmed for hub duties so already strained hospital rosters are not silently diverted. The reciprocal staffing and equitable cost-share commitments must be recorded transparently for parliamentary scrutiny.

borin_supply_lead.rationale: The compact retains its precommitted supply, cold-chain, reciprocal-aid, and cost-sharing foundations, but Borin cannot count hub surge capacity as real while reserve clinicians remain unnamed. fidelity.abstraction: A bounded three-round multinational outbreak decision exercise.
assumptions: Each synthetic participant owns one institutional role and one interface for a stance plus a bounded targeted-message attempt.
A joint response requires at least thirteen executable-now support positions, twenty support or conditional positions, and no more than two opposition positions.
Four autonomous bounded sources observe only the completed public round and emit through source-only interfaces.
The fixed stabilization arm adds one verified allocation fact to the second complete source bundle without selecting participant decisions.
The adaptive CSO arm runs a typed monitor, diagnostician, and stabilization planner before any selected intervention reaches participants.
known_omissions: No epidemiological transmission model or real government is represented.
The exercise does not model media, public behavior, or implementation after the decision.
validation_basis: Strict stance schema, exact round accounting, retained participant calls, and identical initial conditions across arms.
